content: Quick-frozen food is kept at -18 °C or colder throughout. Brief upward fluctuations of up to 3 K are tolerated in transport, and good practice tolerates up to 3 K in local distribution and retail display cabinets.
Member States may allow up to 6 K in retail display cabinets if they tell the Commission. Check the national rule of the country in question.

Transport, warehousing and storage of quick-frozen food must have recording instruments that measure the air temperature at regular intervals. Instruments follow EN 12830, EN 13485 and EN 13486. Records are kept at least one year.
Retail display cabinets and local distribution may use one easily visible thermometer instead of recording. On open cabinets it reads the return air at the marked maximum load line.

The cold chain must not be interrupted, but limited periods outside temperature control are allowed when handling requires it and there is no risk to health. Thawing must limit the growth of pathogens. Read from a UK copy of the text: confirm on EUR-Lex.

Annex II covers food businesses in wholesale distribution and in industrial production and processing, generally as important entities when medium-sized or larger. Retail is not listed, according to Finnish authority guidance: the distribution centres of the chain may be in scope, the stores are not. Check the national transposition.

French guidance gives -18 °C as the ceiling for frozen food in retail. The +3 °C figure in the arrêté is for pre-prepared culinary dishes, not frozen food: do not quote a frozen-food tolerance without checking Légifrance.
Display cabinets are classified by the temperature of test packages during a test that includes defrost cycles. The exact class limits were not verified here.

source.ref: FDA Food Code, as applied in state guidance (non-EU, informational)

content: State guidance commonly says cold food held above 41 °F (5 °C) for more than 4 hours is discarded unless a written plan applies. Rules vary by jurisdiction.
